children: fell slightly after reporting its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 financial results post-market on Wednesday.
For the quarter ended September 30, the application delivery and security provider reported adjusted earnings per share of $4.42 versus the consensus estimate of $4.26.
Revenue for the fourth quarter increased 13% year over year to $917M, which was more than the $885M estimate. Its non-GAAP operating margin of 33.7% was basically in line with the 33.8% estimate.

Looking ahead, F5 expects its first quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to range from $4.25 to $4.37, with a midpoint of $4.31 falling below the $4.38 estimate. The company expects revenue to range from $875M to $895M. The midpoint of $885M clears the $877M estimate.

For the entirety of fiscal 2027, F5 guided for adjusted EPS to range from $18 to $18.30, with a midpoint of $8.15, which is more than the $18.03 consensus. F5 expects revenue to increase by 8% to 9% in fiscal 2027. Revenue increased 10.5% year over year in fiscal 2026.

"Frontier AI is rewriting the rules of enterprise security, accelerating vulnerability discovery to machine speed, expanding the attack surface through APIs and AI agents, and collapsing the time available to respond," said F5 CEO François Locoh-Donou. "F5 is focused on ensuring our customers can meet this moment, using AI to identify risk earlier, and enforcing consistent protection at runtime across every environment."
The F5 Board of Directors also approved an additional $1.5B to its share buyback program. The program had $332M remaining before the new authorization.

title: F5 dips as fiscal 2027 revenue guidance shows slight deceleration
